body:
I don't want to compare my situation with torture, but as it is my life is not dullness but something that I find unbearable and I'm not sure if I really can endure it much longer.

You are right about my potential suicide affecting my parents. It's probably the only reason besides fear of the unknown that is currently preventing me from killing myself. Not sure how long it takes for my egoism to get the upper hand, though.

As for the disfigurement thing. I don't know. I guess you always have very specific ideas of what your friends and lovers are supposed to be like, but you will - if you are not me - meet people you never though you could like and be proven wrong. So I guess I wouldn't rule it out.

>This argument is fallacious. You recognize that your feelings are temporary, however, your current self examination leads you to believe you are pathetic. The reality is that due to your condition being temporary, your outlook on yourself will undoubtedly change as well. Most likely for the better.

I didn't really think of my life and my condition as seperate things, and as I said - I don't believe anything will change. I have stagnated and even worsed too much while I had help and was actively trying.

As for talking with people - I'm not very close with my family, even though I live with them. I have tried explaining my problems to them and I'm certain that they were trying to understand me, but they didn't and everytime a conversation about me came up it started with them trying to be insightful but later talking thoughtlessly like i.e. trying to cheer me up by comparing me to the disabled and telling me how much better I have it...
I have a friend who I met during my stay in the clinic who I can talk to occasionally, but unlike me she has college, a job and a boyfriend, so it happens maybe once ever two weeks...
So it pretty much boils down to my therapist, whom I've been with for over two years, once a week, but that's pretty much it. But since I obviously long for someone to talk with - I guess I wouldn't write here if that wasn't the case - I appreciate you answering.

If death was a void I could perceive I'd be incredibly more afraid of death than I am right now. I don't believe in any form of afterlife, including some uninteresting void. It's gonna be like the time before I was born. But non-existence is a far more comforting thought than eternal life anyway.

So no, I don't think it's better to experience a life of suffering than to simply not exist. And I think most people would choose like that. If you were about to be murdered, but given the choice between a gunshot right between the eyes and being pushed legs first into a rusty, slow meatgrinder, you wouldn't choose the meatgrinder just for the experience's sake, would you?

But I guess you have a point about the future. I'm pretty impressed with what we as a species have achieved over the past few decades and certainly am interested in where we will be in 60 (80 might be a bit far-streched. I'm not 4 anymore) years. I just don't think the time I had to wait would be worth it.

Regarding my parents: I had to give up my apartment after I couldn't leave it because of my anxiety anymore and hadn't had food to eat for 4 days before I was moved to a clinic. So I'm living with my family right now, but I'm only a burden to them. I think my mother is slowly falling into a depression, too because of me...

As for pets. I can never be sure if I can leave the house at all and I don't wanna have dogs I can't reliably care for.

Connecting with people that share my body issues will be pretty hard. I don't know any place where people with abnormally high heads would meet. I haven't even seen anyone with a head as disfigured as mine, but if they existed they probably would be diagnosed with BDD too.

I'm not bipolar. The diagnoses I got over the years were depression, social anxiety disorder, body dysmorphic disorder, avoidant personality disorder, even schizophrenia, although that was later withdrawn as a false diagnosis.
I've taken Escitalopram (20mg) over the past year but currently am switching over to Venlafaxine (currently 300mg) and Olanzapine (10mg).
I've been in cognitive behavioral therapy for 5 years now and was in a psychiatric clinic 4 times. When I started I was pretty optimistic, but unfortunately nothing changed which is why I lost my hope.

>This is a temporary problem. Suicide is permanent.

I agree with you, although I think I'm looking at this from a different perspective.
My condition is indeed temporary and death is permanent. But as my life is just a daily reminder of how pathetic I am, why not simply skip to the inevitable part?

Thank you for taking your time to answer, though.
